definition: A quantity with both a magnitude (size) and a direction, drawn as an arrow and written in bold, such as $\boldsymbol{v}$, or as $\overrightarrow{AB}$.
A quantity with a magnitude only and no direction, such as a mass, a length or a real number $k$ that multiplies a vector.
The vector from the origin O to a point A, written $\overrightarrow{OA} = \boldsymbol{a}$; its components are the coordinates of A.
A vector describing the move from one point to another, such as $\overrightarrow{AB} = \boldsymbol{b} - \boldsymbol{a}$.
The unit vectors $\boldsymbol{i}$, $\boldsymbol{j}$ and $\boldsymbol{k}$ along the $x$-, $y$- and $z$-axes, so that $\boldsymbol{v} = v_{1}\boldsymbol{i} + v_{2}\boldsymbol{j} + v_{3}\boldsymbol{k}$.
The vector $\boldsymbol{0}$ with every component 0: it has no length, and $\boldsymbol{v} + \boldsymbol{0} = \boldsymbol{v}$.
Non-zero vectors where one is a scalar multiple of the other, $\boldsymbol{w} = k\boldsymbol{v}$; they point the same way if $k > 0$ and opposite ways if $k < 0$.
Lying on one straight line; points A, B and C are collinear when $\overrightarrow{AC} = k\overrightarrow{AB}$ for some scalar $k$.
The length of a vector, $\lvert\boldsymbol{v}\rvert = \sqrt{v_{1}^{2} + v_{2}^{2} + v_{3}^{2}}$; it is never negative.
A vector of magnitude 1; the unit vector in the direction of $\boldsymbol{v}$ is $\frac{\boldsymbol{v}}{\lvert\boldsymbol{v}\rvert}$.
